actions: flexes elbow (prime mover, active regardless of forearm pronation/supination position, unlike biceps)

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.innervation_branch: musculocutaneous n. main trunk (+ minor radial n. sensory-motor overlap described in some cadaver studies)

neuromuscular_junction_zone.location_description: mid-belly endplate band -- for where this band lies along the muscle, see motor_endplate_zones

functional_compartments.function_note: Largest cross-sectional area of the elbow flexors; deep to biceps.
functional_compartments.source: Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity musculoskeletal model; Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

motor_endplate_zones.reference_line_from: the proximal end of the arm segment (acromion)
motor_endplate_zones.notes: The clinic's own landmark for the same target is 4-6 cm proximal to the lateral epicondyle, where the radial nerve runs along the humerus and the muscle's maximum thickness lies medial to it. The source states the location as 'the distal third of the arm', which is rendered here as 67-100% of that segment. That is arithmetic on the source's own words, not an inference about the anatomy; no narrower band is claimed than the source gave.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part II -- Proximal Upper Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(6):276 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17060276 -- review synthesis of the intramuscular neural arborization literature it cites (Yi, Li, Yang, Moon and others)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity musculoskeletal model

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transverse on the anterolateral arm at the distal third, about 4-6 cm proximal to the lateral epicondyle.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Superficial to the humeral cortex; biceps brachii lies medial to it at this level.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: The radial nerve is the landmark: it runs along the humerus here, and the muscle's zone of maximum thickness is seen medial to it. Biceps brachii, medial to brachialis, can be confirmed dynamically by asking for forearm supination.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Part I's strategy is the context: brachialis is injected as the only pure elbow flexor, sparing biceps brachii and brachioradialis so that supination is preserved.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Diaconu S et al.
